questions.stem: Find the equation of the tangent line to the circle x^2 + y^2 = 25 at the point (3, 4).
questions.solution: The slope of the tangent line is equal to the negative reciprocal of the derivative of y with respect to x at the given point. The equation of the circle can be rewritten as y = √(25 - x^2). Taking the derivative, we get dy/dx = -x / √(25 - x^2). At (3, 4), the slope is m = -3 / √(25 - 9) = -3 / 4. The equation of the tangent line in point-slope form is y - 4 = -3/4(x - 3). Simplifying gives 4x - 3y = 7.
